title: Low-Cost, Air-Processed Quantum Dot Solar Cells via Diffusion-Controlled Synthesis

source_inventory.title: Low-Cost, Air-Processed Quantum Dot Solar Cells via Diffusion-Controlled Synthesis
source_inventory.scope: The author and independent auditor each read all ten main and six SI pages as text and original-page images: PbO/TAA synthesis, growth series, ZnO preparation, ITO cleaning, device assembly and ligand variants, characterization, storage and historical cost contexts. External cited full recipes and unprinted plot values remain excluded.
source_conflicts: Main p.3 Section 2.2 reports PbO as 232 mg and 1 mmol. Both printed values are retained; no stoichiometric correction is substituted.
Main p.2 Figure 1a labels argon and 40–100 °C; the main p.3 procedure states nitrogen and 40–120 °C. These source statements remain unresolved.
SI p.3 Figure S1 caption says c=60 °C, d=75 °C and e=90 °C, while visible TEM panel letters are left d, middle c, right e. Panel identity is not silently reordered.

Main p.4 Section 2.3 names immersion of PbS–TBAI in the top-layer exchange solution, whereas Figure 1b on p.2 depicts spin-cast PbS–OA layers before EDT or MPA exchange. This source-description difference is retained.
Table 1 prints a literal plus sign in at least one secondary term for this device family; it is preserved instead of silently converted to ±.
Main p.7 prose states Voc values between 0.43 and 0.45 V, whereas Table 1 reports 0.46 V for the TAA–EDT family.
SI p.5 Figure S4 plots FF in panel c and PCE in panel d, whereas its caption assigns PCE to c and FF to d. Both assignments remain visible.
SI Table S2 lists TAA at 99% for cost estimation, whereas the main Materials section lists 98% for synthesis. The grades belong to different source contexts.

SI Table S2 reports TAA: 500 g, $218 and $0.562 unit cost; (TMS)2S: 500 g, $8354 and $14.14 unit cost. These printed numbers are retained despite arithmetic inconsistency; no corrected cost is substituted.
Main p.7 says TAA–EDT has the highest electron lifetime and TMS–EDT the lowest, then gives the opposite printed rank at 0.25 V. Both statements are preserved without reversing the inequality.

Main PDF p.7 / printed 36307 describes an excitonic-peak interpretation reaching up to 82% for the TAA–EDT device family. Figure 5d on main PDF p.6 / printed 36306 shows the high response in the visible region and a smaller peak near 1000 nm. The spectral assignment of the prose 82% statement is unresolved; 82% is not assigned to the near-IR peak and no numerical plot height is digitized.
limitations: No inferred physical batch identity among source-associated samples.
No raw curve digitization, measured atomic coordinates or training eligibility.
Source figure reuse permission remains unverified.

figures.label: Figure 5a-f
figures.caption_paraphrase: Original Figure 5a-f. Panel a: TAA–EDT forward/reverse scans. Panel b: the three device families. Panel c: seven TAA–EDT devices. Panel d: TAA–EDT and TAA–MPA EQE with a solar reference. Panels e–f: three-family decay and lifetime comparisons. EQE interpretation remains unresolved: p.7 describes an excitonic-peak interpretation reaching up to 82%, while panel d places the high response in the visible region and a smaller feature near 1000 nm. No 82% value is assigned to that near-IR feature and no numerical height is digitized.
